_purpose: Current actionable work discovered during verified sessions — not project history. Resolved items are removed here (their resolution is recorded via the commit that removes them + PROJECT_STATUS.md/LESSONS.md if reusable), not accumulated forever. This is separate from PROJECT_STATE.json's next_phase/next_action, which tracks the one current phase-level priority, not the backlog of smaller items surfaced along the way.

items.title: _resolve_safe_path() gives a misleading error for foreign-drive-letter paths (e.g. 'D:foo')
items.reason: During V3 correctness review, a path like 'D:foo' (different drive than REPO_ROOT) was correctly rejected but reported as 'symlinks are not allowed', which is factually wrong even though the security boundary holds.
items.evidence: Empirical probe during V3 review: tools._resolve_safe_path('D:foo') raised RepoToolError('symlinks are not allowed') instead of a drive/traversal-specific message.
items.verification_required: Re-run the same empirical probe and confirm the new error message accurately describes the rejection reason; confirm the path is still rejected either way.

items.title: tools.py's own security boundary has no test file calling it directly (coverage now exists only via downstream consumers)
items.scope: new test file under agent/ (e.g. test_tools.py), no production code changes
items.reason: Originally: zero automated coverage existed. Now substantially mitigated: agent/test_mcp_server.py and agent/test_write_tools.py exercise traversal/absolute/symlink/secret-name rejection through tools._resolve_safe_path indirectly (via MCP and the write boundary), and this indirect coverage caught a real bug (see LESSONS.md: secret-name check skipped for new files). Remaining gap: no test calls tools.read_file/list_repository_files/search_code/_resolve_safe_path directly, and redaction is only verified via rag_index's wrapper, not tools.read_file itself.
items.evidence: agent/test_write_tools.py and agent/test_mcp_server.py collectively exercise the shared security boundary through two different consumers; no agent/test_tools.py exists.
items.verification_required: A test file exists calling tools.py functions directly (not through a consumer) for traversal/symlink/absolute-path/redaction, and passes.

items.title: MCP Streamable HTTP transport has never actually been run/tested (only coded/documented)
items.scope: agent/mcp_server.py only, no production code changes
items.reason: mcp.run(transport='streamable-http', ...) is the documented path for a future hosted multi-tenant platform, but only stdio has been exercised so far (via mcp_demo.py's in-process Client). An untested code path could be silently wrong when we actually try to host it.
items.evidence: agent/mcp_server.py's docstring documents the streamable-http invocation; no test or run has exercised it in this session.
items.verification_required: Start the server with transport='streamable-http' and confirm a real HTTP-based MCP client (not just in-process) can discover and invoke tools, before this transport is relied on for hosting.

items.title: qa-evaluator custom subagent was not available as a subagent_type in a session that predated its creation
items.scope: verification only, no production code changes expected
items.reason: During Architecture V2 Shadow Trial #1 (docs/ARCHITECTURE_V2_EVALUATION_PLAN.md), invoking the Agent tool with subagent_type='qa-evaluator' (.claude/agents/qa-evaluator.md, added in the immediately prior task) failed with 'Agent type not found' -- worked around by having a general-purpose subagent read and follow that file's instructions directly. Root cause confirmed (not just suspected): custom subagent definitions load once at session start; both prior sessions (Trial #1 and Trial #2) were long-running sessions that started before/without a reload after the file existed in a state the harness's project-scan picked up. A genuinely fresh Claude Code v2.1.268 session in this repo lists qa-evaluator natively in its available-agent-types system reminder from the first turn.
items.evidence: Fresh-session probe (2026-09-11): Agent tool invoked with subagent_type='qa-evaluator' and a trivial read-only task ('report the latest V2 trial number without changing any files'). Result returned as a genuinely separate subagent context: it self-identified in its own reply as 'the qa-evaluator subagent' with the exact prescribed duty from .claude/agents/qa-evaluator.md, used only its allowed tools (Read/Grep, 4 tool_uses, 22186ms), and reported real findings (highest trial = Trial #2) with correct source citations. This is direct evidence of native separate-context execution, not a general-purpose fallback silently answering in the requested persona.
items.verification_required: DONE: native invocation confirmed live in a fresh session; the subagent's own self-reported identity plus tool-call telemetry is the proof.

items.title: Complete historical Usage session system -- verified via real browser E2E + independent qa-evaluator
items.reason: P0_PROMPT.txt Sections 19-23, 30-32: Usage must show ALL captured historical sessions (not just today), grouped by Europe/Berlin date, paginated to the earliest known session, with a dedicated /usage/session/{id} detail route. e2e/usage.spec.js drives a real Chromium browser through the session history list and three real session detail pages (known-cost Workbench run, aggregate-only V2 trial, no-token reconstructed session) -- passing both locally and against production. Building this suite found and fixed a real production defect: usage.html/learn.html referenced their CSS/JS via relative paths, which 404'd (and crashed the page with 'Unexpected token <') on any DIRECT navigation to a nested route -- invisible to client-side pushState navigation and to every prior HTTP-status-only check. Fixed by making all asset references absolute.
items.evidence: agent/test_session_history.py (15/15), agent/test_web_server.py::SessionHistoryRouteTestCase (5/5), e2e/usage.spec.js (4/4 Playwright, local AND production), independent qa-evaluator PASS verdict (2026-09-11).

items.title: Session-level token/cost economics -- verified via real browser E2E + independent qa-evaluator
items.reason: P0_PROMPT.txt Sections 24-26: a session's tokens/cost must be honestly labeled (EXACT/AGGREGATE_ONLY/NOT_CAPTURED for tokens, ACTUAL/COST_UNAVAILABLE-with-reason for cost), and must never contradict the same run's figures shown elsewhere. Real Owner-found defect fixed this task: cost_display_label now gives one of 4 canonical states, and a new Usage-level cost_coverage_summary was added (known cost total, sessions with known/unknown cost, coverage %) -- sourced from the same canonical run_usage_summary events. Verified via a real Chromium browser (Playwright, local + production) confirming a known-cost session shows real tokens/ACTUAL cost, an aggregate-only session shows 'aggregate only' with no fabricated $0, and a not-captured session shows NOT CAPTURED/COST UNAVAILABLE. Independent qa-evaluator re-verified all three states directly against the live API and rendered DOM.

items.title: Session value/quality/comparison-to-cohort -- verified via real browser E2E + independent qa-evaluator, Quality now genuinely distinct from Evidence Coverage
items.reason: P0_PROMPT.txt Sections 27-29 plus a real Owner-found defect fixed this task: the top summary previously showed a single conflated 'QUALITY / 100% coverage' figure. quality_score is now honestly None/'NOT SCORED' (this project has no composite quality algorithm), structurally separate everywhere from evidence_coverage_pct (which legitimately differs per session -- verified live: 100%/HIGH_CONFIDENCE for a rich-evidence run, 0%/LOW_COVERAGE for a thin-evidence one). Comparison enriched with wall-time and human-intervention-rate alongside tokens/cost, all gated on >=3 comparable sessions. Verified via a real Chromium browser (Playwright, local + production) confirming 'Quality' and 'Evidence Coverage' render as two visibly separate stats and comparison metrics beyond a bare cohort-size sentence are shown. Independent qa-evaluator re-verified this exact distinction against the live rendered page.

items.title: Browser-level automated regression suite (Playwright) -- established as the project's new quality gate
items.reason: Owner directive: 'Owner manual review should verify product quality, not discover basic deterministic defects.' Smallest robust Playwright Test setup added -- resilient role/text/scoped-class locators, built-in auto-waiting/web-first assertions, no arbitrary sleeps. Usable locally (auto-starts the dev server via webServer config), against an already-running server, or as read-only smoke verification against production (PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL env var, never touches the local server in that mode). Immediately found a real, serious production defect (relative asset paths breaking every nested Learn/Usage route on direct navigation) that every prior HTTP-status-only verification in this project's history had missed.
items.evidence: 13/13 tests passing locally and 13/13 against production (2026-09-11); independent qa-evaluator ran this exact suite itself against production as part of its own verification and confirmed the same result.

items.title: NEEDS_OWNER_DECISION: a real transient production 502/timeout was observed during independent QA, self-recovered, root cause not established
items.reason: The native qa-evaluator subagent, while independently verifying Phase 1+2 against production (2026-09-11), observed a real HTTP 502 Bad Gateway from Railway's own edge on /learn after a ~300s hang, followed by several minutes of request timeouts, with general internet connectivity confirmed fine throughout. Production self-recovered; an immediate rerun of curl, the Python suite, and the full Playwright suite all passed cleanly. Root cause NOT established -- plausibly an unrelated Railway platform event, OR the burst of ~13 concurrent Playwright browser sessions (used for this task's own verification) straining the backend. This is evidence worth the Owner's attention, not a contract failure (uptime/resilience under concurrent E2E load was not one of the stated acceptance criteria) and NOT something this autonomous task should decide how to address (could imply needing Railway plan changes, backend concurrency limits, or simply monitoring -- all business/infrastructure judgment calls).
items.evidence: qa-evaluator's own verification report (2026-09-11, task 'Independent QA of Phase 1+2 fixes') -- observed via direct curl against the real production edge, includes response headers (server: railway-hikari, x-railway-edge: ams1).
items.verification_required: Owner decision: investigate Railway logs around the observed timeframe, and/or decide whether to bound Playwright's local worker concurrency when it might run against production in the future (currently unbounded via playwright.config.js's default parallelism).
